newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq complains that U.N. inspected religious sites.
newsitem.headline: Iraq complains that U.N. inspected religious sites.

text.p: Iraq has complained to the United Nations Security Council about a U.N. arms inspection of Iraqi churches and monasteries, the Iraqi News Agency (INA) said on Thursday.

It said an arms team belonging to the U.N. Special Commission (UNSCOM) in charge of overseeing Iraq's prohibited weapons had committed a "flagrant aggression" when it inspected three churches and convents on the outskirts of Baghdad.
"Foreign Minister Mohammed Saeed al-Sahaf sent a letter to chairman of the Security Council explaining Wednesday's behaviour of the Special Commission and its chairman," INA said.
Sahaf urged the Council to "put an end to such unprovisional and untechnical behaviour followed by the Special Commission".

But in New York, UNSCOM chairman Rolf Ekeus complained to the Council that Iraqi authorities were repeatedly blocking his team's work to find and scrap Iraq's weapons of mass destruction under terms of the 1991 Gulf War ceasefire.

Sahaf said he was "shocked to hear Ekeus' statement on which he distanced himself from the vicious act committed by the inspection team against houses of worship in Baghdad, stressing the team had implemented an order from Ekeus".
The Iraqi press on Thursday accused UNSCOM of engaging in espionage activities against Iraq for the United States.
"We say that the Special Commission...is nothing but a spying system...for America," said al-Thawra, the newspaper of the ruling Baath party.
